groups.why: Both rows check the same Delete button and CRUD Status D Flag on the same Active-column screen, and both expect Delete to remove only new rows and show no D Flag on existing rows.
Both rows edit a value and then restore the original, and both expect the edit (M) status to clear on restore.
The other merged-cell Delete row (V-3c38de72) also expects a Delete response-time limit, so its expected result differs and this row stays alone.
Besides the merged-cell D display, this row expects Delete to respond within a time limit, so no other row has the same expected result.
This row expects existing rows to show D and be deleted from the DB on Save, which differs from the Active-screen rule where existing rows show no D Flag.
This row combines the Insert required-field check and success-toast check with no D Flag on Delete, so it checks different elements and expects different results than the other rows.
This row deletes a row right after input, expects D or cancel, and checks that bulk save has no SQL Error, so its state and expected result differ.
This row checks moving users between the left and right grids by double-click and saving them, which is a different element from CRUD Status display.
This screen rule covers status display after delete, merged rows and cancel all at once, so its target is wide and it can't be matched exactly to one specific row.
This is a comparison-table trace row whose check is a different kind of thing, so it isn't grouped with any measurement row.
